parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**EcoTech Solutions (ETS)**

ETS is a medium-sized technology company based in Country X that specialises in developing eco-friendly smart home devices. Founded in 2010, ETS has grown steadily and now employs 250 people. The company's main products include energy-efficient thermostats, water-saving shower systems, and solar-powered garden lights.

ETS currently sells its products primarily through its website and a network of independent retailers in Country X. The company has been profitable for the past five years, with revenues reaching £15 million and profits of £2 million in the last financial year. However, rising costs of raw materials and increasing competition in the domestic market have put pressure on profit margins.

The Board of Directors is considering expanding into neighbouring countries to increase sales and spread risk. They believe there is growing demand for eco-friendly home technology in these markets. However, this would require significant investment in marketing, distribution, and possibly new manufacturing facilities.

ETS prides itself on its eco-friendly ethos and has won several awards for its innovative products. The company uses locally sourced materials where possible and has implemented a recycling programme for its products. However, the proposed expansion could potentially increase the company's carbon footprint.

The Human Resources Director has suggested that if the expansion goes ahead, they should use a mix of internal promotions and external recruitment to staff the new operations. She believes this approach would provide opportunities for existing staff while also bringing in new expertise.

As ETS considers this strategic decision, it must weigh the potential for growth against the risks and challenges of entering new markets. The company also needs to consider how to maintain its commitment to sustainability while expanding its operations.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following two options for ETS to add value to its products.

- Improve product quality by using more expensive, highly durable materials.
- Enhance brand image through an extensive marketing campaign.

Which option should ETS choose? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following[ insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/ecotech-solutions-ets.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Improving product quality by using more expensive, highly durable materials could increase customer satisfaction. ETS already uses locally sourced materials **[Ap]**, so using higher-quality ones aligns with their eco-friendly ethos and differentiates their products from competitors. This could justify higher prices, offsetting rising raw material costs **[An]**. However, more expensive materials would increase production costs, reducing profit margins in the short term. Also, customers may not be willing to pay higher prices, especially in new markets **[An]**

Enhancing brand image through an extensive marketing campaign could increase awareness of ETS's eco-friendly products. This could support their expansion plans into neighbouring countries **[Ap] **and attract environmentally conscious customers. A strong brand image could also justify premium pricing **[An]**. However, a large marketing campaign would be expensive and might be immediately effective. There's also a risk of being perceived as "greenwashing" if the campaign isn't carefully managed **[An]**

ETS should choose to improve product quality **[E]**. This option aligns better with their core values and award-winning reputation for innovation **[Ap]**. It would support their expansion plans by offering superior products in new markets **[E]**. While initially more expensive, it would likely lead to long-term customer loyalty and could justify higher prices, helping to maintain profitability despite rising costs. This option also carries less risk than a major marketing campaign in unfamiliar markets **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
>

**GHI Cosmetics**

GHI is a medium-sized manufacturer of beauty products based in Country Y. The business was established 20 years ago and has grown steadily. It now employs 200 people in its factory and head office. GHI specialises in mid-priced organic skincare and makeup products. All items in the product range are packaged in brightly-coloured recycled plastic containers and are targeted at environmentally conscious young consumers.

GHI uses a range of social media channels, which include popular podcasts that provide guidance on the application of makeup products. These are shared widely, and GHI makes use of feedback and viewer comments to improve existing products and develop new ones. It also shares new product launches with online followers.

The beauty industry has become increasingly competitive in recent years, with many new entrants focusing on natural and sustainable products. GHI's sales have grown slowly over the past two years (see Appendix 1). The CEO is considering expanding the product range to include a line of vegan hair care products to boost sales and attract new customers. She is also looking for a suitable celebrity to act as the face of its brand.

GHI currently sells its products through department stores and specialist beauty retailers. In some larger outlets, brand representatives are employed to offer advice and demonstrations to consumers. It is investigating the possibility of selling directly to consumers through its own website and social media channels to increase profit margins.

The government of Country Y has recently introduced new regulations requiring all cosmetics companies to list full ingredients on packaging and reduce waste. GHI is evaluating the potential impact on its production costs and manufacturing processes.

**Appendix 1: GHI Financial Data**

| Year | Revenue (\$m) | Profit (\$m) | Units sold (000’s) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 2021 | 38.5 | 4.2 | 1,540 |
| 2022 | 40.1 | 4.4 | 1,604 |
| 2023 | 41.8 | 4.5 | 1,672 |

Explain **two **ways GHI adds value to its beauty products.

parts.solution_md:
GHI adds value to its beauty products through branding **[K]**. GHI's products are packaged in brightly-coloured recycled plastic containers **[Ap]**. This attractive and environmentally friendly packaging creates a strong brand image that appeals to GHI's target market of environmentally conscious young consumers **[An]**. This means that GHI can charge higher prices for its products **[An]**

GHI also adds value through offering convenience **[K] **to customers. GHI employs brand representatives in some larger outlets to offer advice and demonstrations to consumers **[Ap]**. This personalised service helps customers use GHI's products effectively **[An]**. By providing this extra service, GHI can justify charging premium prices compared to its competitors who don't offer assistance **[An]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think the most important purpose of business activity is always to add value? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Adding value is important if a business wants to make a profit **[K]**, as it involves increasing the difference between the costs of making a product and the price it can be sold. If a business does not make a profit, it is unlikely to survive in the long term** [An]**

Meeting customer needs **[K]** is also important. If customers are not satisfied with a business's products, they may choose to buy from competitors, reducing business sales and making it difficult to break even **[An]**

Adding value is not always the most important purpose of business activity, especially for less established business start-ups **[E]**. It is more important to meet customer needs so they buy products repeatedly. This may involve lowering prices or increasing quality, which could actually reduce added value in the short run. Once brand-loyal, adding value to make a profit may be more important to ensure the long-term survival of a business **[E]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Adding value: Increases the difference between cost of production and selling price [k]; helps the business generate profit [an]; without profit, a business may not survive in the long term [an]
>   - Meeting customer needs: Providing products or services that satisfy demand [k]; if customers are unhappy, they may switch to competitors [an]; loss of customers can reduce sales/revenue and threaten survival [an]
>   - Making a profit: Businesses need profit to reinvest, grow or reward investors [k]; no profit means the business may not be able to operate long-term [an]
>   - Survival: Especially important for new or small businesses [k]; focus might be on covering costs rather than adding value at first [an]
>   - Social/ethical aims: Some businesses prioritise sustainability or social impact [k]; these aims might reduce short-term profit or added value [an]
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Adding value is important for generating profit [k]; however, for start-ups, meeting customer needs may be more important to ensure repeat sales and survival [eval]
>   - A business may need to reduce prices or increase quality to attract buyers, even if this lowers added value [eval]
>   - Once brand loyalty is built, the business can then focus more on adding value to improve profit and ensure long-term success [eval]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

**Extract:**

Sports Safety Equipment (SSE) 

SSE manufactures sports safety equipment in country Z. It is a public limited company which has been successful for over 30 years. The main product SSE manufactures is safety helmets for different sports, such as bicycle riding, cricket and skateboarding. SSE has one large factory making the safety helmets. The factory uses flow production. The production workers each specialise in one task on the production line. SSE’s raw materials are imported. SSE sells its helmets in several other countries and is planning to expand into many more. It will need to carry out market research before entering new markets in other countries. Each country has different sports that are popular and the style of helmets varies from country to country. SSE plans to build its own factories in its most important markets in other countries and will need to choose a suitable source of finance. The Human Resources Director has decided to use internal recruitment for the managers of the new factories. There will need to be effective communication between the managers of the new factories and SSE’s head office in country Z. Most of SSE’s sales in country Z are through sports equipment shops. Customers like to try on the helmets to check they fit correctly. SSE currently sells its helmets in other countries through its website. SSE is also increasing its product range. The latest new product being developed is a children’s cricket helmet.  

Appendix 1 Extract from SSE’s website 

If you want the best protection when playing sport then buy an SSE safety helmet! We supply a wide range of safety helmets for you when playing sport. Whatever the sport - SSE produces a helmet for you. You can order directly from this website by entering your head measurements below. Get the perfect fit for you! 

Appendix 2 

Email from SSE’s Managing Director to SSE’s Finance Director To: Finance Director From: Managing Director 

Date: 1 September 2023

 Re: Demand for SSE’s products 

Demand for SSE’s products in country Z is forecast to increase. Our government has imposed import tariffs on safety helmets. We may be able to increase our prices. The exchange rate in country Z is expected to fall. However, other countries have introduced import quotas on safety helmets. We will have to consider all the likely effects of these changes.

Explain **two **advantages of using specialisation when producing SSE’s products.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Specialisation keeps unit costs low **[K] **because performing one task repeatedly makes workers quicker, allowing lower prices to be charged **[An] **for SSE's range of sports safety helmets **[Ap]**. This makes them more competitive than their rivals **[An]**

Specialisation is likely to lead to higher quality **[K] **as workers become skilled at one particular task. This may improve SSE's reputation as a reliable supplier** [An] **of this crucial equipment, leading to increased sales to retailers or sports clubs **[Ap]**, enhancing confidence in the safety of the products **[An]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Build an X → Y → Z chain of reasoning, linking a series of consequences to fully develop your analysis
> - For example, specialisation leads to higher quality (X) which improves SSE's reputation (Y), resulting in higher sales (Z)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two full paragraphs, one for each reason/point In each paragraph:
> 
>   - State one valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain how it works using a cause–effect chain → up to 2 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant advantages might include:
> 
>   - Increases efficiency/productivity—it allows the use of more machinery and technology in the production process—increases output per production employee
>   - Time is saved during the production process—as workers do not need to move around between tasks on the production line—improves the use of space in the factory so can fit in more production lines into the limited space
>   - Helps keep (unit) costs low; only performing one task makes workers quicker – allowing lower prices to be charged
>   - Cheaper to train each employee – as production employees are trained in only one task

>   - Higher quality – as workers become more skilled at one particular task
